extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, stakeholders, and members of the public who may review or comment on EPA rulemaking for power plant greenhouse gas standards
extracted.subtask_description: Information and procedural guidance for engaging with EPA's proposed repeal of greenhouse gas emissions standards for fossil fuel-fired electric generating units under CAA section 111, including how to find rule text, supporting analyses, and participate in the public hearing. Useful to commenters, regulated industry, state/local agencies, and legal/technical reviewers preparing submissions or testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket identification and reference
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing or submitting materials, reference the docket number EPA-HQ-OAR-2025-0124 so submissions are associated with the correct rulemaking. The page lists the docket number prominently under 'Basic Information.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the Rule Summary and Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: On June 11, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin proposed to repeal all “greenhouse gas” emissions standards for the power sector under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act. This proposal would ensure affordable and reliable energy supplies and drive down the costs of transportation, heating, utilities, farming, and manufacturing while boosting our national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the summary language to understand the administration's stated objectives and rationale for the proposed repeal; tailor comments or analyses to directly address these stated goals and the legal basis under CAA section 111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing participation and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA held a virtual public hearing on July 8, 2025, from 8:00 AM - 7:00 PM (ET) on the proposed repeal. Registered Speaker List in Approximate Speaking Order (pdf) and a YouTube live link are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To participate or review testimony: consult the registered speaker list, watch the hearing recording, and contact SPPDpublichearing@epa.gov if you need assistance. Use hearing records when preparing comments or replies and cite specific testimony when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the rule history for context
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule History entries document key dates and prior actions (e.g., Proposed Rule 06/11/2025; Notice of final action denying or partially denying petitions 01/08/2025; Final Rule for NSPS 04/25/2024; Supplemental Notice 11/20/2023; prior Proposed Rule 05/23/2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the rule history to trace prior decisions, supplemental notices, extensions, and related proposals to ground legal, technical, or factual arguments about consistency, precedent, or changed circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Supporting Information and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Resources lists materials such as: Fact Sheet (Proposed Repeal), Regulatory Impact Analysis for the Proposed Repeal, Regulatory Text: Primary Proposal, Regulatory Text: Alternative Proposal, Supporting Information for Petitions for Reconsideration, and Supporting Information for the Final Carbon Pollution Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on the provided PDFs (e.g., RIA, regulatory text, fact sheets) as primary sources for technical, economic, and legal claims in comments. Cite specific sections, tables, and regulatory text in submissions; compare primary and alternative regulatory texts where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track agency announcements and planned timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements note actions such as 'Trump EPA Announces Reconsideration...' and state intended rulemaking schedules (e.g., proposed reconsideration in Spring 2025 and final rule by December 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor announcements for updated schedules and scope changes; align comment timing with open comment periods and public hearings. Use announced timelines to plan supplemental analyses if a supplemental notice or extension is likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage related program pages for broader context
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to related Stationary Sources of Air Pollution pages and programs (e.g., New Source Performance Standards, NESHAP, Good Neighbor Plan) are provided for context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these related pages to understand how this rule interacts with other stationary source regulations, compliance programs, and sector-specific guidance; reference relevant cross-program obligations or conflicts in substantive comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact points for help and inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need assistance, contact the SPPD Public Hearing Team by email: SPPDpublichearing@epa.gov. 'Contact Us About Stationary Sources of Air Pollution' links are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided contacts to resolve procedural questions about participation, obtain accessibility accommodations for hearings, or clarify where to submit materials; document any agency correspondence cited in filings.
